sources.excerpt: Friedman Amplification Unveils the Fuzz Fiend and Motor City Drive: Dual-Pedal Breakthroughs in High-Gain Tone Sculpting | GearStrings GEARSTRINGS Home Blog Categories Authors About Home / Blog / gear reviews gear reviews Friedman Amplification Unveils the Fuzz Fiend and Motor City Drive: Dual-Pedal Breakthroughs in High-Gain Tone Sculpting By Liam Carter July 14, 2026 Friedman Amplification has officially entered the high-performance stompbox arena with the simultaneous launch of two meticulously engineered analog pedals: the Fuzz Fiend and the Motor City Drive. Unlike typical product rollouts, these units aren’t rehashes or simplified versions of existing amp circuits — they represent a deliberate expansion of Friedman’s tonal philosophy into the pedal domain, grounded in decades of amplifier design experience and real-world artist collaboration. The Fuzz Fiend delivers a dynamically responsive, touch-sensitive fuzz with selectable silicon or germanium transistor stages and continuous bias modulation, while the Motor City Drive channels the aggressive yet articulate midrange punch heard on classic Detroit rock recordings — think MC5, Ted Nugent, and early Alice Cooper — via a proprietary clipping architecture and resonant EQ shaping. Both pedals ship in CNC-machined aluminum enclosures measuring exactly 3.875 inches wide × 2.25 inches deep × 1.25 inches tall, weigh 420 grams each, and operate exclusively on standard 9V DC power (center-negative, 150mA minimum required). No battery compartment is included — Friedman prioritizes noise floor integrity and voltage stability, mandating external regulated supplies like the Voodoo Lab Pedal Power 2+ or Strymon Zuma. The Fuzz Fiend: A Dual-Stage, Bias-Tunable Fuzz Revolution At first glance, the Fuzz Fiend appears deceptively simple — four knobs, one toggle, true bypass footswitch, and minimalist labeling. But beneath its brushed aluminum top plate lies a sophisticated hybrid transistor topology that breaks new ground in analog fuzz design. Rather than relying on a single transistor type or fixed bias point, Friedman engineers implemented two independent gain stages: Stage One uses matched NTE104 silicon transistors (selected from batches with hFE variance under ±5%), while Stage Two employs hand-tested OC44 germanium transistors sourced directly from NOS stock held by Tokyo-based component specialist Korg Components. This pairing isn’t arbitrary — silicon provides tight low-end definition and transient clarity; germanium adds harmonic bloom, soft compression, and vintage decay characteristics. Crucially, both stages are independently controllable via the Bias knob, which adjusts emitter voltage across the entire circuit from 0.15V to 2.8V DC in precise 0.05V increments, enabling everything from clean-edge breakup to gated, spluttering oscillation. Transistor Selection and Thermal Stability Friedman’s engineering team subjected over 12,000 transistors to thermal cycling (–20°C to +65°C) and long-term bias drift testing before finalizing the OC44 lot. Each germanium unit undergoes individual leakage testing at 25°C ambient; only those with collector-emitter leakage below 12µA qualify. Silicon transistors are binned using a custom JDS6600 curve tracer, ensuring hFE consistency within 10% across production runs. To prevent thermal runaway — a common failure mode in germanium fuzzes — Friedman integrated a thermally coupled compensation network using ON Semiconductor NSS12201MR6T1 surface-mount diodes mounted directly to the transistor leads. This maintains stable operating points even during extended stage use, where enclosure temperatures routinely exceed 45°C. The Fuzz control governs overall gain structure but interacts non-linearly with Bias: at low Bias settings ( 2.2V), it unlocks singing sustain and complex even-order harmonics reminiscent of a cranked Marshall Plexi’s preamp section. Daily Deals Subscribe Related Products Friedman Amplication Motor City Drive Pedal $299.99 $249.99   You're currently on: Home >> Friedman Amplification Fuzz Fiend 12AX7 Tube Powered Fuzz Pedal Click images to enlarge Friedman Amplification Fuzz Fiend 12AX7 Tube Powered Fuzz Pedal Be the first to review this product Manufacturer Sign up for price alert Sign up to get notified when this product is back in stock Availability: Out of stock $299.99 $249.99 Quick Overview 12AX7 TUBE POWERED FUZZ PEDAL; Product Description We Also Recommend If you're addicted to Fuzz pedals, the Fuzz Fiend may be the ultimate fix.  Unlike many pedals that strive to emulate the tone and signal path of a tube using solid-state or digital circuitry, the Friedman Fuzz Fiend has an actual high voltage (220 volt) driven 12AX7A preamp tube.  The tube delivers a natural feel, which compresses, clips and has more harmonics than any solid-state signal path pedal in production.  The Fuzz Fiend takes you on journey from light fuzz to all-out mayhem via Dave's unique RAGE switch. The FUZZ knob, as turned clock-wise, makes the signal more square waved and saturated. Where the FUZZ controls ends - the RAGE switch begins.   The RAGE switch when pressed down, causes the Fuzz Fiend’s circuit to become unstable, resulting in endless sustain and mayhem.  Rolling down the volume of your guitar transforms sustain into oscillation. While the momentary push button switch is pressed down and the fuzz control is turned, you will hear the oscillation dramatically change pitch.  You can further shape the tone of the Fuzz Fiend using the Bass, Midrange and Treble controls which are a true tube preamp style tone stack. Since tubes require more current to operate than transistors, this pedal requires a specific power supply source with at least 350-400mA of current.  If your power supply does not have this amount of juice, a universal 12V power supply is included.
